hints: Notice that radium is in Group 2, so think about how other Group 2 nitrates like magnesium or barium nitrate behave on strong heating.
Remember that all Group 2 nitrates decompose to the same three types of products: a metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.
Check which equation gives the correct Group 2 oxide formula, RaO, and is fully balanced for Ra, N and O atoms.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 2 pattern**

Great start, you spotted radium is below barium in Group 2. That means it will react just like calcium, strontium and barium nitrates.

General pattern:
$$2\text{M(NO}_3)_2(s) \rightarrow 2\text{MO}(s) + 4\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$

**Apply it to radium**

Simply put Ra in place of M. Radium is +2, oxygen is -2, so the oxide must be $\text{RaO}$, not $\text{Ra}_2\text{O}$.

Expected change:
$$2\text{Ra(NO}_3)_2(s) \rightarrow 2\text{RaO}(s) + 4\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$

**Check balancing and conclude**

Count atoms on both sides. Left: 2 Ra, 4 N, 12 O. Right: 2 Ra in 2RaO, 4 N in 4NO2, and O = 2 + 8 + 2 = 12. It balances perfectly, so this is the correct thermal decomposition.

options.A: This gives $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{O}_2$ as gases. That is the decomposition pattern for Group 1 nitrates like $\text{NaNO}_3$ which give nitrite then oxide, not for Group 2 nitrates which give $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$.
options.B: This gives $\text{N}_2$ gas as a product. Nitrates do not decompose to nitrogen gas on heating. The nitrogen-containing product for Group 2 is brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas, so this equation is chemically incorrect.
options.C: This is exactly the Group 2 nitrate decomposition: metal oxide + nitrogen dioxide + oxygen. It has the correct oxide $\text{RaO}(s)$ for a Group 2 metal and is fully balanced with 2 Ra, 4 N and 12 O on each side.
options.D: This gives $\text{Ra}_2\text{O}$ as the solid. That oxide formula is wrong for Group 2. Since Ra is +2, it forms a 1:1 oxide $\text{RaO}$, like $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{BaO}$. $\text{M}_2\text{O}$ is a Group 1 oxide pattern.
